summary:
Our project, SideQuest, is an interactive educational game designed to introduce young learners to space exploration and the responsibilities of astronauts. We developed a game where players must successfully complete six different levels of challenges to reach a satellite and establish communication with Earth. Along the way, players encounter quizzes and interactive tasks that test their knowledge, problem-solving, and understanding of space-related concepts.

Our solution addresses the NASA challenge by turning astronaut training into an engaging, game-based learning experience. Instead of simply reading about space missions, users get to experience a simplified version of an astronaut's journey through interactive challenges.

This project is important because it makes learning about space more fun, accessible, and engaging for younger audiences. It encourages curiosity about science, technology, engineering, and space exploration while helping children develop critical thinking and problem-solving skills.
details:
SideQuest, is an interactive educational game designed to introduce young learners to space exploration and give them a simplified experience of what it takes to become an astronaut. The game takes players through a six-level mission in which they must successfully complete different challenges to reach a satellite and establish communication with Earth. Throughout the mission, players encounter quizzes and interactive tasks that test their knowledge, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills. Each level brings them closer to achieving the main objective of the mission.

The project addresses NASA's Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge by turning the concept of astronaut training into an engaging and educational gaming experience. Instead of simply reading about space exploration, users get to participate in a simulated mission where they learn while playing. The game makes learning about space more enjoyable and encourages young people to become curious about science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM).

One of the major benefits of our project is that it combines education with entertainment. It encourages users to think critically, make decisions, solve problems, and apply their knowledge to complete each level. Our intended impact is to make space education more accessible and inspire younger generations to develop an interest in space exploration and STEM-related careers. We hope the game can motivate children to explore scientific concepts and see themselves as potential future astronauts, scientists, or engineers.

We developed the game using Java and CSS, which helped us build its functionality and design its visual interface. We also considered how to make the game easy to understand, engaging, and suitable for younger audiences. Our team focused on creating a clear progression between the six levels, balancing educational content with enjoyable challenges, and ensuring that the game remained connected to the NASA challenge.

What makes our project creative is the way it transforms astronaut training into an interactive mission. The six-level structure gives players a specific goal to work towards, while the quizzes and challenges make learning part of the adventure. Throughout development, we considered accessibility, user engagement, educational value, difficulty progression, and ease of navigation. Ultimately, our goal was to create more than just a game; we wanted to create an experience that makes young learners excited about space and encourages them to see learning as an adventure.
